observation.visible_scene: First-person 360-degree (equirectangular) view from a rider on an enclosed water slide. The rider's feet, in black water shoes, sit at the bottom center of the frame, pointing forward. The tube ahead is translucent and lit with a green/cyan glow, and it ends in a fork: two circular openings (left one bright white, right one bright cyan) divided by a dark central wall. A horizontal projection seam crosses the mid-frame, separating the dark blue upper region from the slide below. Water ripples/bubbles cover the slide floor between the feet and the openings. The 'Attractions 360°' watermark is fixed at bottom right.
visible_changes: The rider moves forward continuously through the tube: the two fork openings gradually enlarge and the tube walls spread toward the frame edges from the first to the last frame.
The dark central divider between the two openings shifts in apparent shape and position, consistent with changing perspective and moving reflections rather than a separate object moving.
The water surface on the slide floor shows ongoing ripple/bubble motion frame to frame, indicating flowing water under the rider.

The rider's feet remain anchored at the bottom center with only minor bobbing/rotation relative to the frame; the change in view is dominated by forward translation, not by the feet moving across the image.
No editing cut is visible; the geometry change is smooth and continuous across the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Which branch (left or right) the rider will take at the fork, since the segment ends before reaching it.
The start of the slide and any events after this excerpt.
The exact slide speed and the rider's body posture above the camera.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent enlargement of the openings is purely forward translation or partly a slight camera rotation, as background cues are limited inside the tube.
The material identity of the tube (assumed translucent plastic/fiberglass from appearance only).
The precise cause of the divider's shape changes (perspective vs. reflection vs. water distortion) cannot be separated definitively.

camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
